Notes

Advice about finding your own voice curdles into gossip, compulsory quiet and shared secrets. The final miracles would require the ordinary world to reverse itself.

没有心思再去胡思乱想

心思 and 胡思乱想 repeat 思, thinking, but give it different forms: attention available for a task versus thoughts running out of control. The line says there is no energy left even for overthinking. That tired precision opens a song full of instructions about what to hear, say, ignore and keep secret.

  • Lyric transcript
勾心斗角

勾心斗角 means competitive maneuvering and intrigue. The speaker declares himself beyond its “age,” treating scheming as an immature phase one should outgrow. Yet the advice that follows assumes a world full of hostile speech. The opening is less a claim that conflict has disappeared than an attempt to choose a different posture within it.

  • Genius community transcript
出门在外

出门在外 means being away from home, where familiar protection and rules no longer apply. 要多加小心 has the sound of advice offered before somebody leaves. The next warning is about listening rather than physical danger, so the main hazard of the outside world becomes other people’s words.

  • Lyric transcript
舌头很多口水乱喷

People disappear into tongues and saliva. The sentence makes gossip physically excessive before it names any particular accusation: there are simply too many mouths producing too much material. It also makes the following wish for one’s “own voice” concrete. A voice carries a person; these disembodied tongues mostly produce spray.

  • Lyric transcript
自己的声音

The advice permits movement: go out, see the world, enjoy its scenery. Its condition is to keep your own voice. This is not a demand for isolation or purity. It allows curiosity while resisting the pressure to become another version of the surrounding chatter, a distinction that gives the track’s title its tension.

  • Lyric transcript
不干净

干净 moves easily from physical cleanliness to an unblemished moral record. “Everyone is the same” first sounds conciliatory, then becomes an accusation that nobody is innocent. The shift checks the speaker’s earlier authority too: a song warning about other people’s speech includes itself in the compromised crowd.

  • Lyric transcript
乖乖的坐成一排

乖乖 is the affectionate but controlling language of telling children to behave. The orderly row prepares the later classroom question, bringing school discipline into a song about speech. What begins as the sensible wish for less gossip now risks becoming a demand that everyone be quiet and obedient.

  • Lyric transcript
脱裤子放屁

脱裤子放屁 is a deliberately ridiculous image of doing an unnecessary extra step. It often works as the first half of a saying whose answer is simply 多此一举, needless effort. Here the missing explanation is supplied by the comic picture itself. After several measured lines of advice, that bodily vulgarity punctures the speaker’s almost elder-like tone.

  • Genius community transcript
乌烟瘴气

乌烟瘴气 combines dark smoke with foul, unhealthy air, and describes a disordered or morally unpleasant atmosphere. The translation gives the social effect; the Chinese still pictures something one has to breathe. It also lets the crude fart joke contaminate the whole surrounding space.

  • Lyric text
我们都知道

A secret everyone knows is not hidden information; it is information governed by an agreement not to say it aloud. The next lines wait for someone else to raise the question in class. That turns the classroom into a small social system where knowledge can be common while the risk of speaking is left to another person.

  • Lyric transcript
铁树开花

铁树开花 is an idiom for something exceptionally rare; the “iron tree” names a cycad rather than a tree made of metal. The next example, the sun rising in the west, shifts from extreme rarity to the reversal of ordinary nature. Pairing them turns hopeful waiting into a joke about how impossible the desired change feels.

  • Taiwan Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency: cycads
  • Genius community transcript
太阳从西边升起来

The expression is used for a reversal so surprising it would overturn the normal order of things. 案例, “case” or “example,” gives this impossible event a dry, almost report-like label. After wishing for a miracle, the voice briefly sounds as though it could enter one in a file and wait for precedent.

  • Lyric transcript

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
